+[[smnip-handler]]
+==== Example: Handler code for nested preemption
+
+This section introduces several pseudo-code examples for handling interrupts in the presence of Smnip.
+Ssnip examples can be constructed analogously by using the equivalent S-mode CSRs.
+
+===== Direct mode SW dispatcher
+
+The first example modifies the example handler from AIA by adding support for nested preemption.
+This handler assumes `mtvec.mode` = Direct (0).
+In this mode, all traps have a common entry point, and thus all interrupts use a common SW dispatcher.
+
+[,c]
+----
+save processor registers
+i = read CSR mcause
+if (i >= 0) {
+    handle synchronous exception i
+    restore mstatus if necessary
+}
+if (mstatus.MPIE == 1) {
+    save mistatus
+    loop {
+        i = read CSR mtopi
+        IPRIO = (i & 0xFF)
+        write IPRIO to mithreshold  /* raise threshold */
+        id = i>>16
+        enable interrupts
+        call the interrupt handler for major interrupt id
+        disable interrupts
+        restore mistatus
+        write mistatus.pithreshold to mithreshold /* restore threshold */
+    }
+}
+restore processor registers
+return from trap
+----
+(This example can be further optimized, but with an increase in complexity.)
+
+The most important difference compared to not using Smnip is that interrupts are enabled before calling the interrupt handler.
+While the interrupt is handled, a pending-and-enabled higher-priority interrupt can preempt the currently running interrupt handler.
+
+It is necessary to raise the threshold after reading {mtopi},
+because a higher priority interrupt could have become pending after the trap was taken.
+
+Restoring the threshold after the handler call returns
+allows lower priority interrupts to be handled
+without restoring and saving the processor registers.
+
+In case an interrupt an interrupt ceases to be pending before {mtopi} is read,
+this is a spurious interrupt.
+It can occur for level-sensitive interrupts.
+To handle those, a spurious interrupt handler needs to be installed for interrupt id 0.
+
+===== Direct mode SW dispatcher including external interrupts
+
+The handler needs to be extended for efficient handling of external interrupts,
+if external interrupts are prioritized among each other.
+The example below assumes that the top external interrupt can be read and claimed via {mtopei}.
+
+[,c]
+----
+save processor registers
+i = read CSR mcause
+if (i >= 0) {
+    handle synchronous exception i
+    restore mstatus if necessary
+}
+if (mstatus.MPIE == 1) {
+    save mistatus
+    loop {
+        i = read CSR mtopi
+        id = i>>16
+        if (id == MEI) {
+          i = read CSR mtopei
+          eid = i>>16
+          handler_addr = ei_handlers[eid]
+        } else {
+          handler_addr = i_handlers[id]
+        }
+        IPRIO = (i & 0xFF)
+        write IPRIO to mithreshold  /* raise threshold */
+        enable interrupts
+        call the interrupt handler at handler_addr
+        disable interrupts
+        restore mistatus
+        write mistatus.pithreshold to mithreshold /* restore threshold */
+    }
+}
+restore processor registers
+return from trap
+----
+
+===== Vectored mode SW dispatcher
+
+This example further modifies the example handler by considering `mtvec.mode` = Vectored (1).
+In this mode, some interrupts may share a common SW dispatcher,
+while others (higher priority interrupts) are handled in dedicated handlers (referred to as fast interrupt handlers here).
+
+In a system based on this example, fast interrupts must be able to preempt other interrupts.
+Because the fast interrupt handlers are not guaranteed to comply with the psABI,
+it must also be guaranteed that the common SW dispatcher does not dispatch fast interrupt handlers.
+
+Any fast interrupt handler must be configured to a nested interrupt priority that is higher than interrupt using the common SW dispatcher.
+
+In this example, it is assumed that exceptions have an entry point on traps that is different from interrupts.
+
+[,c]
+----
+save mepc, mistatus
+enable fast interrupts (mfie = 1)
+save processor registers
+
+loop {
+    i = read CSR mtopi
+    IPRIO = (i & 0xFF)
+    write IPRIO to mithreshold  /* raise threshold */
+    id = i>>16
+    enable interrupts (mie = 1)
+    call the interrupt handler for major interrupt id
+    disable all interrupts (mie = 0 -> mfie = 0)
+    restore mistatus
+    write mistatus.pithreshold to mithreshold /* restore threshold */
+    enable fast interrupts (mfie = 1)
+}
+
+restore processor registers
+disable fast interrupts (mfie = 0)
+restore mepc, mistatus
+return from trap
+----
+(This example can be further optimized, but with an increase in complexity.)
+
+In this example, fast interrupts are enabled for an extended period.
+After saving the minimal state needed to resume after preemption,
+fast interrupts are being enabled.
+Enabling fast interrupts has the highest urgency.
+
+This allows fast interrupts to preempt the dispatcher.
+Because of that, {mtopi} can never report a fast interrupt.
+
+Interrupts can still be globally enabled before calling the interrupt handler,
+to ensure that other interrupts, that are not fast interrupts, 
+but have a higher nested interrupt preemption priority can preempt the currently executing handler.
+
+While restoring the threshold before the next loop iteration,
+all interrupts have to be disabled.
+As writing zero to {mie} also clears {mfie},
+fast interrupts need to be enabled afterwards.
+
+[[smnip-handler-vectored-external]]
+===== Vectored SW dispatcher including external interrupts
+
+This section builds upon the two handler examples introduced previously.
+
+[,c]
+----
+save mepc, mistatus
+enable fast interrupts (mfie = 1)
+save processor registers
+
+loop {
+    i = read CSR mtopi
+    id = i>>16
+    if (id == MEI) {
+      i = read CSR mtopei
+      eid = i>>16
+      handler_addr = ei_handlers[eid]
+    } else {
+      handler_addr = i_handlers[id]
+    }
+    IPRIO = (i & 0xFF)
+    write IPRIO to mithreshold  /* raise threshold */
+    enable all interrupts (mie = 1)
+    call the interrupt handler at handler_addr
+    disable all interrupts (mie = 0 -> mfie = 0)
+    restore mistatus
+    write mistatus.pithreshold to mithreshold  /* restore threshold */
+    enable fast interrupts (mfie = 1)
+}
+
+restore processor registers
+disable fast interrupts (mfie = 0)
+restore mepc, mistatus
+return from trap
+----
+(This example can be further optimized, but with an increase in complexity.)
+
+
+Assembly version:
+
+[source,asm]
+----
+    .if XLEN == 64
+        .equ REGSZ, 8
+        .macro sr reg, off, base
+            sd \reg, \off(\base)
+        .endm
+        .macro lr reg, off, base
+            ld \reg, \off(\base)
+        .endm
+        .macro shxadd dst, idx, base
+            sh3add \dst, \idx, \base
+        .endm
+    .else
+        .equ REGSZ, 4
+        .macro sr reg, off, base
+            sw \reg, \off(\base)
+        .endm
+        .macro lr reg, off, base
+            lw \reg, \off(\base)
+        .endm
+        .macro shxadd dst, idx, base
+            sh2add \dst, \idx, \base
+        .endm
+    .endif
+
+.equ MEI_ID,           11
+.equ CSR_MISTATUS,     0x346
+.equ CSR_MITHRESHOLD,  0x347
+.equ CSR_MIPREEMPTCFG, 0x348
+.equ MSTATUS_MIE,      8
+
+interrupt_dispatcher:
+    addi    sp, sp, -(2*REGSZ)
+    sr      s0, 0*REGSZ, sp
+    sr      s1, 1*REGSZ, sp
+
+    csrr    s0, mepc
+    csrr    s1, CSR_MISTATUS
+    csrsi   CSR_MIPREEMPTCFG, 1  /* enable fast interrupts */
+
+    call    __riscv_save
+
+dispatch_loop:
+    csrr    t0, mtopi
+    srli    t1, t0, 16
+    li      t2, MEI_ID
+    bne     t1, t2, int_irq
+
+ext_irq:
+    csrr    t0, mtopei
+    srli    t1, t0, 16
+    la      t3, ei_handlers
+    shxadd  t3, t1, t3
+    lr      t3, 0, t3
+
+have_handler:
+    csrw    CSR_MITHRESHOLD, t0  /* raise threshold */
+
+    csrsi   mstatus, MSTATUS_MIE
+    jalr    t3
+    csrci   mstatus, MSTATUS_MIE
+
+    csrw    CSR_MITHRESHOLD, s1  /* restore threshold */
+
+    j       dispatch_loop
+
+int_irq:
+    la      t3, i_handlers
+    shxadd  t3, t1, t3
+    lr      t3, 0, t3
+    j       have_handler
+
+dispatch_exit:
+    call    __riscv_restore
+    csrci   CSR_MIPREEMPTCFG, 1  /* disable fast interrupts */
+    csrw    mepc, s0
+    csrw    CSR_MISTATUS, s1
+
+    lr      s0, 0*REGSZ, sp
+    lr      s1, 1*REGSZ, sp
+    addi    sp, sp, (2*REGSZ)
+    mret
+----
+
+
+[[smnip-fast-handler]]
+===== Preemptible Fast Interrupt Handler
+
+An example of a preemptible fast interrupt handler is
+
+[,C]
+----
+fast_interrupt_handler:
+  save mepc, mistatus
+  enable interrupts
+
+  /* interrupt handling */
+
+  disable interrupts
+  restore mepc, mistatus
+  return from trap
+----
+
+As part of the interrupt handling, the pending bit needs to be cleared by software.
+
+It is expected that GNU toolchains will preemptible C-handlers like
+
+[,C]
+----
+void fast_interrupt_handler() __attribute__((interrupt("preemptible")))
+{
+
+  /* interrupt handling */
+
+  return;
+}
+----
+
+Context needed to return after preemption is saved before enabling interrupts.
+Interrupts are enabled before executing the first statement of the function.
+Before returning, interrupts are disabled, and context is restored.
+
+
